target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures describe the dividend rate structure for specific series. 2023 D406 identifies Series A as floating and Series C, L, O as fixed. 2024 D393 identifies Series A as floating and Series C, L, O, P, Q as fixed. The shared topic is the classification of dividend rates by series, with 2024 expanding the list of fixed-rate series.

Both disclosures describe the dividend rate structure for 'all other Series'. 2023 D406 states 'Dividends on all other Series are based on a fixed-to-floating rate.' 2024 D394 repeats this exact statement for 'all other Series'. This is a direct correspondence on the residual category of dividend rates.

comparisons.peer_topic: Series E preferred stock dividend and redemption terms
comparisons.peer_summary: Series E preferred stock, issued as depositary shares, pays semiannual fixed dividends until May 15, 2025, followed by quarterly floating rate dividends, with dividends payable only when declared by the Board. Series V, related to this series, was redeemed in its entirety on January 30, 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and C disclose specific dividend structures for preferred stock series that utilize a fixed-to-floating rate mechanism. MS describes a general policy where 'all other Series' (beyond specific fixed-rate ones) are based on a fixed-to-floating rate. Citi provides concrete examples, such as Series E, where dividends are 'payable semiannually... at a fixed rate until... May 15, 2025, and thereafter payable quarterly... at a floating rate,' illustrating the same fixed-to-floating structure applied to specific series.

comparisons.peer_topic: Redemption of Series K and Series P Preferred Stock in 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, the firm redeemed all outstanding shares of its Series K Preferred Stock ($700 million value) and Series P Preferred Stock ($1.50 billion value), recording a $34 million difference between redemption value and net carrying value as an addition to preferred stock dividends.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS disclose that certain preferred stock series utilize a fixed-to-floating rate structure for dividends. MS identifies Series P and Q (among others) as having a fixed rate, while 'all other Series' are fixed-to-floating. GS explicitly identifies Series K and Series P as 'Fixed-to-Floating Rate Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock,' confirming the existence of this specific instrument type in both entities' capital structures.

sentences.text: Dividends on all other Series are based on a fixed-to-floating rate.

In 2024, the firm redeemed all outstanding shares of its (i) Series K 6.375% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock (Series K Preferred Stock) with a redemption value of $700 million ($25,000 per share), plus accrued and unpaid dividends and (ii) Series P 5.00% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock (Series P Preferred Stock) with a redemption value of $1.50 billion ($25,000 per share), plus accrued and unpaid dividends.
